title: The Best Programming Language for Tokenmaxxing: An Investigation of Coding Agent Behavior Across Programming Languages
abstract: arXiv:2607.22807v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Although coding agents are now very effective in a variety of programming languages, this paper first shows that the cost (in tokens) can very significantly by programming language. We evaluate five recent models on programming problems in Python, Java, Rust, and OCaml. We carefully control for problem difficulty, and show that there can be stark variation in token consumption that is consistent across models. To understand why, we analyze both the structure and content of agent trajectories. First, we re-execute every intermediate solution and abstract each trajectory as a sequence of test-outcome vectors, then label the work between successive solutions. This reveals agents repeatedly producing noncompiling solutions in unfamiliar languages and revising solutions that already pass. translated_title: Token消耗最大化（Tokenmaxxing）的最佳编程语言：编程智能体在不同编程语言下的行为研究
translated_abstract: 尽管编程智能体目前在多种编程语言中都已非常有效，本文首次表明其成本（以Token计）会因编程语言的不同而产生显著差异。我们在Python、Java、Rust和OCaml的编程问题上评估了五个最新模型，并严格控制问题难度，结果显示不同编程语言之间的Token消耗存在显著差异，且这一差异在各个模型中保持一致。为探究其原因，我们对智能体轨迹的结构和内容进行了分析。首先，我们重新执行每个中间解，将每条轨迹抽象为测试结果向量的序列，并对相继解之间的工作内容进行标注，这揭示了智能体在不熟悉的语言中会反复生成无法编译的解决方案，并且会反复修改已经通过测试的解决方案。其次，我们分析轨迹文本，发现智能体会在代码注释中规划解决方案，不信任所提供的测试用例，而更倾向于使用自行构造的输入……（原文此处被截断）
tldr: 编程智能体的Token消耗因编程语言而显著不同且跨模型一致，其原因是智能体在不熟悉的语言中反复生成无法编译的代码并重复修改已通过的解决方案。
en_tdlr: Token costs of coding agents vary significantly and consistently across programming languages, driven by behaviors such as repeatedly generating noncompiling solutions in unfamiliar languages and revising solutions that already pass.
